scope: Actual dispatcher, real indexed session repository and session cache, PostgreSQL main pool max1; stub HTTP and SDK invocation only. No providers or real CLI.
interpretation: L16 remains open: instrumentation and controlled attribution do not resolve the overhead budget breach.

After the bounded scanner fix, the identical actual PG matrix still breached the budget: worst free-miss overhead p99 15 ms and held-miss 48 ms. Scanner microprofile improvement does not demonstrate SQL latency improvement. These are separate local runs; do not subtract their independent percentiles as causal components.

Free indexed-miss overhead p99 of 9 ms is the 280000-byte translated nonstream scenario; its binding p99 is 3.986053 ms. Independent percentile summaries must not be subtracted or summed as per-request causal components.
The 1KB passthrough nonstream free-miss scenario has binding p99 of 5.083681 ms and advertised overhead p99 of 5 ms.
Held 20 ms single-pool connection amplifies misses; warm positive and negative cache hits issue no SQL.
The SDK positive-binding measurement is a separately labelled offline mock exception; it does not measure actual process launch or inference.
Body-read wait, binding wait, advertised overhead, terminal duration and added TTFT remain separate. Binding wait is not subtracted from advertised overhead.
This is local disposable PG18 evidence, not a production deployment or fleet performance claim.
